channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade supports families but strips economic trees
item.description: An environmental agency director says burners are cutting orange and mango trees, leaving land exposed to climate change.

item.title: Finance minister’s critics call for his dismissal over economic hardship
item.description: The CSOs Consortium on Public Accountability says poor inflation control and debt accumulation justify removing Sheku Bangura.

item.title: Analyst says Sierra Leone's vice presidency offers no clear path to succession
item.description: Foday M. Daboh argues that past vice presidents entered office without an independent political base or a route to the presidency.

item.title: Three Namibian women earn 50MIA sports nominations
item.description: Journalists Limba Mupetami and Geneva De Jager and Netball Namibia representative Carol Garoes were nominated across the continental honours.

item.title: Zambian football club bars two fans from all its matches over political symbol
item.description: The supporters were filmed displaying a symbol associated with Zambia's governing United Party for National Development during a match against Nkana FC.

item.title: Morocco sends health minister to Addis Ababa public health conference
item.description: Youns Bjijou leads the Moroccan delegation to the fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa, opened by Africa CDC and Ethiopia's government.

item.title: Benin sets 2027 secondary education budget at 124.838.383.589 francs CFA
item.description: Minister Clément Kouchadé presented a plan that includes teacher recruitment, school repairs and adult education centres.

item.title: Botswana coalition MPs warn of repeat of predecessor's election defeat
item.description: Two years after their historic election victory, some MPs in the Umbrella for Democratic Change (UDC) coalition are raising alarm about its future at the polls.

item.title: French judge places Congo’s presidential aircraft in state custody
item.description: The aircraft, seized in Bordeaux in 2020 during a €2.2 billion dispute with Commisimpex, is expected to be returned to the Republic of Congo.

item.title: Norway urges South Sudan leaders to pursue dialogue and better governance
item.description: Ambassador Roar Haugsdal said emergency aid alone cannot resolve a crisis driven largely by political choices and conflict.

item.title: 1º de Maio do Príncipe wins national title with 3-0 comeback
item.description: The Príncipe island side overturned a 2-0 first-leg loss to 6 Setembro by scoring three times in Sunday's second leg in São Tomé.

item.title: Dakhla's regional services company to sign French development loan for water networks
item.description: French ambassador Philippe Lalliot is in Dakhla on 23 and 24 November, with talks on local services, education and culture also on the programme.

item.title: Kenya's anti-graft commission says it cannot bar election candidates
item.description: Abdi Mohamud says the electoral commission decides eligibility, while his agency checks integrity and sends it findings and recommendations.

item.title: Chapo urges investors to build job-creating projects in Gaza province
item.description: At a conference closing, Mozambique’s president called for investment to deliver employment, income and better living conditions for residents.

item.title: Morocco plans repairs for 32 flood-cut road sections
item.description: The regional equipment director says contracts for flood-damaged roads are expected before December ends, with awarded contractors given up to three months.

item.title: Lutchigadoo asks Mauritius court to cut 18-year drug sentence
item.description: His defence seeks a term of 13 to 15 years, while prosecutors argue the appeal has not shown the sentence was legally wrong.

item.title: Sierra Leone's ROCKCEM invests US$60 million in cement processing and distribution
item.description: The company was building a Songo warehouse and planned a mill designed to produce more than 60,000 50-kilogram bags a day.

item.title: Johannesburg council to elect mayor as coalition deal gives ANC bloc control
item.description: A reported four-party pact includes the ANC, ActionSA, MK and the EFF, with Herman Mashaba in line to lead the city.

item.title: Escola de Samba Tropical plans 1,200-person Isaura Gomes tribute
item.description: The São Vicente group will divide its Carnaval 2027 parade into three sections and estimates preparation costs at 11,900 contos.

item.title: Analysts see Macky Sall backing a deal with Senegal's president
item.description: Two political analysts say the former president is more likely to back Faye's coalition than to return to lead his party.

item.title: Bushiri urges fair hearing for arrested preacher Uebert Angel
item.description: The Malawi-based prophet said Angel should be treated as innocent until proven guilty after his arrest in Zimbabwe.

item.title: Neves wins second Cape Verde presidential term by more than 40,000 votes
item.description: The incumbent widened his 2021 lead over his nearest rival, while abstention remained above 60% in Sunday's vote.

item.title: Cape Verde's parliament receives budget proposal worth 101.7 billion escudos
item.description: The draft projects 5.7% growth and 1.8% inflation, while a technical analysis questions the quality and resilience of those forecasts.

item.title: Minnesota lawmaker urges Kenyan women to contest 2027 election
item.description: Huldah Momanyi, re-elected with 71.8% of votes in Minnesota, made the appeal at a school in Nyamira County.

item.title: Zimbabwe to unify reading programmes under 2026–2030 strategy
item.description: The education ministry is finalising a framework to coordinate literacy interventions for learners from Early Childhood Development through Form 4.

item.title: Authorities close Kanène Ndiob health post, leaving 14 000 without nearby consultations
item.description: The closure followed a protest by residents of 48 villages seeking the replacement of the post’s head midwife, whose care patients criticised.

item.title: Cameroon's universities gain 57 newly qualified senior lecturers
item.description: Cameroon had the largest group of candidates at the 23rd aggregation exam of the African and Malagasy Council for Higher Education, held in Bangui from 10 to 18 November.

item.title: Cameroon's standards agency showcases certification at investment forum
item.description: The agency is presenting standardisation and certification as tools for business competitiveness and access to markets at the Yaoundé event.

item.title: UNESCO office presents 99 collected Cameroonian songs in Yaoundé concert
item.description: The performance followed fieldwork in Adamaoua and East regions and the publication of Polyphonies du Cameroun Vol. 2.

item.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore full diplomatic ties
item.description: Ruto and Tshisekedi reached the agreement at a summit in Oyo, after Kinshasa recalled its envoy and rejected Kenya’s ambassador nominee.

item.title: Ivorian officials urge parents to protect children online
item.description: A data-protection official cited cyberbullying, grooming and privacy breaches, and called for a national observatory on minors’ digital safety.

item.title: Health union And Gueusseum calls 48-hour strike over housing allowances
item.description: The union says contract staff are owed less than CFA32 billion and wants a meeting with the prime minister.

item.title: South Sudan central bank gives unlicensed forex dealers 30 days to comply
item.description: A one-month licensing window will use simplified procedures to register eligible mobile, informal and street-based currency operators.

item.title: TANAPA launches campaign across 21 parks and five heritage sites
item.description: The authority says it will promote lesser-known attractions and encourage Tanzanians to take part in domestic tourism.

item.title: Livingstone High Court nullifies Mulobezi election over Grade 12 certificate
item.description: The ruling found Hastings Sililo lacked the required certificate when nominated for the August 13 parliamentary poll.

item.title: Algeria opens online pre-registration for contract military recruits
item.description: The defence ministry says applications cover the army, air force, navy, territorial air defence, gendarmerie and Republican Guard.

item.title: Fiat opens Grande Panda orders in Algeria from 2 949 000 DZD
item.description: The car is assembled at the company's Tafraoui plant near Oran, with a localisation rate above 20%.

item.title: Djiboutian media creator wins IGAD award for local-language migration work
item.description: Migane Mohamed Megag received the Kampala trophy for work on migration and human mobility produced in a local language.

item.title: Burkina Faso motorcycle tour brings more than 300 riders across eight regions
item.description: The second edition ended in Ouagadougou on Saturday, 21 November 2026, after riders covered more than 1 800 kilometres in eight days.

item.title: Togo plans 1 500 hectares of new farm zones in Kara for 2027
item.description: The state programme also provides for 1 500 hectares of lowlands, support for 155 existing zones and the opening of seven processing centres.

item.title: Rescuers evacuate seven people trapped by River Mubuku in Kasese
item.description: The group, including boys aged 13 and 16, was caught near Katindo bridge as heavy rains raised water levels in western Uganda.

item.title: Guinea court's gold case awaits witness summons for former minister
item.description: Abdoulaye Yéro Baldé was scheduled to testify on 23 November, but a source close to him said he had received no court notice.

item.title: Burkina Faso trains 99 military retirees in farming and livestock
item.description: The three-week course in Ouagadougou covered crop production, animal care and farm management for personnel preparing to leave service.

item.title: Garwe orders councils to cut MPs’ stand prices by 80%
item.description: The local government minister’s circular requires every council to apply the discount and keep records of the stands and payments.

item.title: Women become majority of Rwanda's tertiary students
item.description: Women made up 51.8% of tertiary-level students in 2024, reversing the balance recorded in 2017.

item.title: Bangui school director seeks new classrooms for more than 700 pupils
item.description: Gertrude Dipot Yimandji says the school’s nine classrooms no longer meet demand as enrolment rises.

item.title: Deep Mind and Team Geospark win first prizes at Ivory Coast's extractive industries hac...
item.description: Deep Mind's modular biorefinery turns organic waste into biomethane, carbon dioxide and biofertilisers, while Team Geospark built a filter for acidic mine water.

item.title: Singida anti-graft bureau recovers 1.146 billion/- from project probes
item.description: The bureau monitored 56 development projects worth about 135.32 billion/- across education, health, roads, governance and water from April to September.

item.title: Mchacha rejects reports he is seeking a ministerial post
item.description: The Democratic Progressive Party governor says his work to build support in the Southern Region is aimed at strengthening the party.

item.title: Khumalo and six senior officers seek more than R112 million from state
item.description: The Crime Intelligence chief and his colleagues allege malicious prosecution and unlawful detention after corruption and fraud charges were withdrawn.

item.title: Hichilema commissions 2.5-megawatt solar plant in Monze
item.description: The Chikuni Mission hybrid facility is valued at Three Million United States Dollars, the president said at its commissioning.

item.title: Congo opens 20-hectare Madingo-Kayes farming zone
item.description: The site has solar-powered pumping for irrigation, mechanisation support and four Kavaki vehicles, with vegetables intended for markets in three cities.

item.title: REVIMO claims pouco mais de 210 milhões de meticais in protest losses
item.description: The road network company says the losses were caused by post-election demonstrations it attributes to politician Venâncio Mondlane.

item.title: Egypt takes 32% of Russian tour-package sales in November
item.description: Tourism officials say Egypt's share rose from last year, while Asian destinations compete for Russian visitors.

item.title: Tonj East commissioner urges Unity State inquiry after 23 killed
item.description: The caretaker commissioner says seven children, three women and 13 men died in the nighttime attack at Bol Bol cattle camp.

item.title: Namibia agriculture grows 17.8% as construction contracts
item.description: The farm sector added 0.8 percentage points to second-quarter growth, while construction fell 15.5%, according to the statistics agency.

item.title: Rachedi and Hafez family settle dispute after Cairo home visit
item.description: The Algerian filmmaker visited the late Egyptian singer’s home with his nephew, who said a misunderstanding had been cleared up.

item.title: Liberia’s House rejects US$54.7 million national ID concession
item.description: The rejected deal named OeSD International GmbH, an Austrian subsidiary whose parent-company guarantee and financing source were not disclosed.

item.title: Mali’s special forces free about 30 soldiers near Algerian border
item.description: The operation used combat and transport helicopters, a Sukhoï fighter and drones, according to Bamada.net.

item.title: Ethiopia's digital payments reach ETB 33 trillion in 2025/26
item.description: The National Bank of Ethiopia reported 157.6 million mobile money accounts by June 2026 as digital finance expands across the country.

item.title: Nigerian companies generate more operating cash as profits lag
item.description: An analysis of 19 non-bank members of the Nigerian Exchange's NGX 30 index found operating cash flow outpaced profit growth in the first nine months of 2026.

item.title: COP31 ends without global deal on climate finance sought by Tunisia
item.description: Tunisia estimates $55 billion in climate-finance needs for 2026-2035, including $10.7 billion for water and about $8 billion for agriculture.

item.title: Namibian employers urged to reconsider experience demands for entry-level jobs
item.description: The Namibian argues that people seeking a first opportunity are shut out when even suitable entry-level roles require previous work experience.

item.title: CDC alleges US$50,000 paid to oust MOVEE leader Kemayah
item.description: The opposition party says Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung funded a faction seeking to remove the former foreign minister from party leadership.

item.title: South Sudan starts secondary exams for 53,301 candidates
item.description: The national examinations run through December 1, with candidates from 596 schools, including 1,009 refugees and 4,216 accelerated-programme learners.

item.title: Ghana names 23 for Women’s World Cup playoffs in Morocco
item.description: Coach Kim Lars Björkegren gives Beline Nyarko her first senior call-up ahead of Ghana’s opening match against Ecuador on November 28.

item.title: Nsanganzelu urges Tanzania U-17s to fix slow starts after 2-2 draw
item.description: The coach says his players must carry their stronger second-half performance into the next match after recovering from two goals down.

item.title: Church leader urges Liberia's Legislature to reject current mining infrastructure deal
item.description: Rev. Samuel B. Reeves says the draft lets Bea Mountain Mining Corporation recover costs through tax offsets, with no all-in limit on what Liberia pays.

item.title: Pedebo school’s leaking roof sends pupils home in rain
item.description: More than 300 children attend the government school in Maryland County, where broken walls, scarce desks and no toilets compound the damage.

item.title: Damazin transport fares climb as residents seek to leave
item.description: Bus tickets to Khartoum cost up to SDG 220,000 as fewer vehicles and security fears leave families struggling to find seats.

item.title: Togo's torture victims' association urges release of 22 detainees
item.description: The Association of Victims of Torture in Togo (ASVITTO) says 18 court decisions have not been enforced and asks for detainees' release and compensation before June 2027.

item.title: Tunisia’s feminist movement loses co-founder Amel Ben Aba
item.description: The left-wing activist and journalist, who was imprisoned in the 1970s, helped establish the Tunisian Association of Democratic Women.

item.title: CAF adopts Kiswahili as an official language
item.description: The decision followed a campaign led by Tanzania and was approved by representatives of CAF’s 54 member associations in Abuja.

item.title: Chad’s cyber agency warns students about risks in digital books
item.description: At a N’Djamena university, officials cited malware, phishing and data theft, and explained where victims of online abuse can seek help.

item.title: Guinea gold mining raises concern over mercury exposure among children
item.description: A civil-society activist warns that mercury used at mining sites may enter food, but says health studies are needed to assess exposure and effects.

item.title: Senegal awaits sports tribunal ruling on disputed Africa Cup of Nations title
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport is due to decide by 30 November whether to overturn a ruling that awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory by forfeit.

item.title: Fifth detainee dies in Bangui prison after isolation without medical aid
item.description: Ndayo Gaston was found unresponsive when his cell was opened, after hours in isolation at Ngaragba central prison.

item.title: Madagascar anti-corruption prosecutor seeks warrants for Rajoelina and Ntsay
item.description: The requests follow charges against 13 people over five aircraft registered in Madagascar and transferred to Iran.

item.title: Germany commits €56.5 million to Madagascar projects
item.description: The funding, agreed after talks in Antananarivo, includes €46.4 million for financial cooperation and €10.1 million for technical assistance.

item.title: Ivory Coast and Qatar advance three sports projects
item.description: The plans include an arena in Ébimpé, youth friendship games and cooperation on sports medicine, following talks in Doha.

item.title: Miss and Mister Inter Zonas show to feature 11 São Vicente areas
item.description: The third contest, set for 19 December at Mindelo Technical School's auditorium, will build its four presentations around the colours of Cape Verde's flag.

item.title: Wapinda youth group urges stronger Ebola response as suspected cases top 400
item.description: The group reports 7 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, and says health teams lack fuel, medicines and ambulances to reach patients.

item.title: Juba schoolgirl says fees and transport threaten her university plans
item.description: Nancy Modo, 19, has completed Senior Four at New Apostolic Secondary School in Juba, but says the cost of fees and transport is putting her plan to become a pediatrician at risk.

item.title: Mauritius power board seeks 15 MW to offset Nicolay G2 outage
item.description: The 20 MW gas turbine has been out of service since 19 November, and Indian technicians are repairing it.

item.title: Burundi intelligence agents arrest three Banyamulenge refugees in Bujumbura
item.description: Families say they have heard nothing about the men since their arrest on 20 November, and one was due to marry the next day.

item.title: UNICEF urges Kenya to shield children's services from aid cuts
item.description: Representative Shaheen Nilofer called on national and county governments to prioritise education, healthcare and social support in their budgets.

item.title: Cocoa Capital allocates GH¢3.395 billion for Ghana's cocoa purchases
item.description: The commercial paper, listed in Accra, drew about GH¢3.59 billion in investor demand and will fund the Ghana Cocoa Board's 2026/27 bean buying.

item.title: Chapo visits Mozambique’s central bank to review its work
item.description: The president is due at the Maputo headquarters to examine the bank’s operations and its regulation and supervision of the national financial system.

item.title: Malawi wins seat on 10-member resource governance group
item.description: Frank Tumpale Mwenifumbo says the place will help promote Malawi's rare earths to foreign investors and shape mineral policy.

item.title: Tunisia’s medicines agency puts 50-dinar fee on pharmacies, not patients
item.description: The charge covers administrative review of exceptional orders for treatments not authorised for sale in Tunisia, the agency said.

item.title: Chad bars exam-year students from transferring schools
item.description: The immediate ban covers public and private schools nationwide, including students in the 3e and Terminale classes.

item.title: Central African Republic justice minister challenges BRDC's legal status
item.description: Arnaud Djoubaye Abazene said the opposition coalition lacks official registration, after authorities allowed its 13 November march to proceed.

item.title: Four hopefuls file for Burundi’s 2027 presidential election
item.description: The candidates include two independents and nominees of FPN Imboneza and CNL, the Congrès National pour la Liberté party, with one filing missing a 100 million FBu deposit receipt.

item.title: Nigeria signs Valmont deal for 40,000-hectare irrigation pilot
item.description: The agreement also provides for a factory to make irrigation equipment locally with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure.

item.title: Kamuzu airport operator switches to manual check-in after storm damage
item.description: Airport Development Limited says storm damage to local network infrastructure has disrupted its check-in system, while passengers report long queues and slow starts by staff.

item.title: House committee finds more than 40 defects in $54.7 million registry deal
item.description: Liberia’s lawmakers flagged procurement and biometric-data concerns in a proposed agreement with Austria’s OeSD International GmbH.

item.title: Nigeria's drug agency arrests South African golfer and Kenyan chef over 50.4kg cannabis
item.description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) named the two men, South African professional golfer Grobler Henlo and Kenyan chef Abubakar Njambi, after a cannabis shipment was.

item.title: Uganda researchers estimate 17,000 annual alcohol-related deaths
item.description: A study presented in Kampala puts the yearly economic cost of excessive drinking at USh11 trillion, about $2.95 billion.

item.title: Madagascar’s football federation gives Ajesaia kit and balls
item.description: The club’s U15 side won its category and its U13 team finished second at a junior tournament in Mauritius on 14-15 November.

item.title: Ivory Coast farmers push for national livestock traceability to curb cattle theft
item.description: Breeders at the Abidjan livestock fair want a nationwide system to identify animals, which they say would better address cattle theft and the spread of disease.
